description.value: Cafe Calabria is a long-standing Italian cafe on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, the street once known as 'Little Italy,' built around a custom espresso blend developed by founder Francesco Murdocco over 30 years ago. It has attracted a loyal multi-generational customer base and earned coverage in The Vancouver Sun, The Globe & Mail, Enroute, and numerous other publications. A touring cyclist will find a full espresso bar, Italian paninis, gelato, and warm indoor seating in one of Vancouver's most vibrant and walkable neighbourhoods.

bike_parking_detail: 3 racks within 100m: rack at 42m; wall_loops (3 spaces) at 49m; stands (3 spaces) at 80m. Total: 6 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fully corroborates OSM contact data (address, phone, name). The menu page explicitly lists a Vegetarian panini option. No mention of bike parking, washrooms, Wi-Fi, takeout signage, or water refill appears anywhere on the website or in OSM tags; the website copyright is 2012 and content appears last meaningfully updated during COVID (2020), so absence of amenity information is noted but the business is confirmed open.
concerns: Website copyright reads 2012 and the most recent substantive content update appears to be a COVID-19 notice (circa 2020), suggesting the site is not actively maintained. Amenity information may be incomplete or outdated.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, well-documented, open Italian cafe with decades of media coverage on a major Vancouver cycling corridor. Strong candidate for inclusion.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Menu lists a dedicated Vegetarian panini: 'Grilled eggplant, red onion, bocconcini, mozzarella cheese, lettuce, tomato'; website notes 'We have a Panini for everyone: from meat-lovers to cheese-lovers to vegetarian.'
